# Katalon TrueTest Journeys

This skill covers coverage built from real traffic. TrueTest records user sessions on a linked application. It groups them into journey maps made of flows. You find the flows that users take, check which flows have cases, and queue generation for the ones that do not. Tool names below are bare. Clients add a prefix (Claude Code: `mcp__<server>__<tool>`).

The `true-platform-testing` skill routes end-to-end requests here. Katalon True Platform (formerly TestOps) holds the cases that this skill finds and checks.

## Availability boundary

- **Can:** list the linked TrueTest applications and their tracking environments. Search captured sessions and read one session. Search and read journey maps. Start a journey map build and poll it. Queue case generation from sessions or from one flow.
- **Cannot:** drive the live application or prove that a flow works today. Read sessions older than the 31-day search window. Edit, archive, approve, or retry a journey map. Cancel a queued job. Create requirements.
- **A session shows what users did, not what is right.** Generated cases copy observed behavior, bugs included. Take expected results from a requirement or from the user. Mark the rest "observed, unconfirmed".

Read `references/capability-boundaries.md` when the user asks whether the platform can do one specific operation.

## Resolve context first

1. Call `list_projects`. Use the project the user names. Ask when several fit.
2. Call `list_repositories` when generated cases need a home. Treat repository and Test Project as one target.
3. Call `memory_list` once. Read matching headlines with `memory_read` for naming and folder conventions. Quote a convention. Never present it as a platform fact. If `available` is false, say memory is unavailable. Never call `memory_write` or `memory_forget` here.
4. Call `list_truetest_auts` with `project_id`. The AUT identity is `platform_aut_id` together with `client_code`. If several match, ask the user to choose. If the list is empty, TrueTest is not linked to this project. Say so and stop. Linking happens in the platform UI.
5. Call `list_truetest_tracking_environments` with `client_code`. Ask which environment to use when several exist. Production traffic and test traffic give different maps.
6. Carry `project_id`, `client_code`, and `tracking_environment_id` into every later call. The MCP keeps no state.

Page through `list_` and `search_` results with `page_token` when the first page is not the whole list.

## Pick the starting point

| The user wants | Start here |
|---|---|
| Coverage of a whole journey, or "what do users do that we do not test" | Journey map path (`references/journey-maps.md`) |
| Cases for one behavior, page, or time window | Session path (`references/session-selection.md`) |
| To see what a journey map says | `get_truetest_journey_map`. It reads only. |

## Journey map path

1. Call `search_truetest_journey_maps` with `client_code` and the tracking environment. Filter by `status` `active` and by the tracked-data window the user cares about.
2. Pick the map whose window covers the question. If none fits, offer to build one (step 5).
3. Call `get_truetest_journey_map` with `map_id`. Add `flow_id` to read one flow with its linked cases. Each of the four lists (pages, flows, steps, transitions) has its own page token. Page each one on its own.
4. Compare. For each flow, read what the map reports about coverage and linked cases. Then check the project with `find_test_cases` and `search` (`types` `["test_case"]`) for cases that the map does not link. Sort the flows into covered, partly covered, and uncovered. Rank the uncovered ones by traffic.
5. Build a map only when no suitable map exists. `create_truetest_journey_map` starts an async job. Preview the tracking environment, the time range, any `session_attributes` and `url_keywords`, and the two flags `carry_over_annotations` and `compare_with_previous_map` (both default to true). Get a yes. Call it once. Report the result as queued.
6. Poll the exact `request_id` with `get_truetest_journey_map_request`. When it completes, copy the correlated `map_id` unchanged into `get_truetest_journey_map`. Never pick the map by list order.
7. On a validation error, conflict, timeout, or upstream error, report it. Do not resubmit. After a timeout with no `request_id`, call `search_truetest_journey_maps` with `status` `generating` to find the job before you ask the user what to do.

Read `references/journey-maps.md` for paging, window choice, and how to read coverage.

## Session path

1. Call `search_truetest_sessions` with `project_id`, `client_code`, `start_time`, and `end_time`. Use the narrowest range that answers the question. It spans at most 31 days. Pass `tracking_environment_id` to get attributes, flow metadata, and the replay link.
2. Narrow with `url_patterns`, `attributes`, `minimum_step_count`, and `maximum_step_count`. Use the `email` filter only when the user asks to locate that session, and prefer `session_id` when the user has one. The email value is personal data: never repeat it in the shortlist or the report.
3. Call `get_truetest_session` on each candidate. Drop duplicates of one path, bots, and one-off errors.
4. Build the shortlist table (see "Present before you generate").

Read `references/session-selection.md` for filters, paging, and triage rules.

## Present before you generate

Show the user what you plan to generate from. Use this table for sessions. Keep it to 25 sessions or fewer.

| UTC | Steps | Duration | Session ID | Custom attributes | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Show custom attributes as compact JSON. Show duration in a human form. Show the replay value as a link. Leave an unavailable value visibly empty. Add a one-line summary per session and the cases it would yield.

For a flow, name the flow. Say whether it already has linked cases.

## Generate

1. Get a yes that names the exact sessions or the exact flow. This yes is on top of the write policy in `references/write-policy.md`.
2. A flow that already has linked cases follows the backend regeneration behavior. Say so and confirm again.
3. Call `create_truetest_test_case_from_session` once with 1 to 25 `session_references`. Or call `create_truetest_test_case_from_flow` once with `map_id` and `flow_id`. Pass every reference and ID exactly as a tool returned it. Never build one.
4. `STARTED` means queued, not complete. For the flow tool, `TERMINATE` means no request was created. Report that and ask. Do not retry on your own.
5. Wait, then read back. Flow path: `get_truetest_journey_map` with `flow_id`. Session path: `find_test_cases` and `search` for the new cases. Recent cases may need a few minutes to appear. Do not assume a folder.
6. Treat every generated case as a draft. Check its type and name. Hand off for refinement.

Read `references/generation-and-review.md` for outcomes, read-back, and the draft checklist.

## Privacy

Sessions come from real users. Never copy names, emails, account numbers, or free text into a case, a report, or chat. Use reserved values such as `@example.com` addresses. `include_raw_events` returns up to 100 events with field values unredacted. Set it only for an explicit troubleshooting request. Check the output before you reuse any value.

## Report

State the AUT and environment, the map or session window, how many flows or sessions you reviewed, which flows were covered, which were queued for generation, and what you read back. Name what remains uncovered.

## Hand-offs

- Refine generated cases, split them, and link requirements: `create-test-cases`.
- Place cases in folders and suites, and audit traceability: `test-management`.
- Values, fixtures, and cleanup for the cases: `test-data`.
- Decide what to cover first across a release: `test-plan`.
- Run the cases: `execute-test`.

### references/capability-boundaries.md

<!-- GENERATED from shared/references/capability-boundaries.md - edit the source -->
# Katalon MCP Capability Boundaries

Contract source: the live Katalon True Platform MCP server, 74 tools, captured 2026-10-20. Older docs pages list other names. If a tool named here is missing in your session, say so and use the closest tool your client discovered. Never call a tool name from memory. At session start, compare this list with the tools your client discovered. If they differ, trust the discovered set and say which names changed.

Name tools by bare name, as written here. Clients add a prefix. Claude Code uses `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

## Available

Workspace and discovery
- `list_projects`, `list_repositories`, `find_iterations`, `find_execution_profiles`.
- `search` runs semantic search over test cases, suites, folders, requirements, and uploaded specification documents.
- No tool returns the signed-in user. Take the user from the client session. Ask the user for any assignee UUID.

Requirements and ALM
- `find_requirements`, `read_requirement`. Requirements are a read-only mirror of Jira or Azure DevOps.
- `find_test_cases_by_requirement`.
- `manage_requirement_test_case_linkages` links or unlinks, many requirements to many cases, in one call.
- `list_alm_integrations` returns the integration and connection IDs. `fetch_defects` shows the defects already linked to a result, a case, or an execution. `create_defect` files a new one.

Test cases, folders, suites
- `find_test_cases`, `read_test_cases` (many IDs per call), `create_test_case`, `update_test_cases` (batched actions), `move_test_case`, `duplicate_test_case`, `delete_test_case`.
- `find_test_folders`, `manage_test_folder`.
- `find_test_suites`, `read_test_suite`, `manage_test_suite`.
- `find_test_suite_collections` reads collections. No tool creates or edits a collection.

Execution
- `read_auts`, `create_test_run` (manual and automated), `update_test_run` (CONFIGURE, START, END), `read_manual_ai_session`.
- `create_manual_ai_session` is the legacy launcher for a subset of cases. Prefer `update_test_run` with START and `KATALON_AI`.
- `build_run_configuration`, `build_schedule`, `build_private_local_testing_config`.
- `rerun_execution` reruns an automated execution.
- `list_schedule`, `read_schedule_detail`, `update_schedule_configuration`.

Results and evidence
- `find_test_results` reads results by test result, by execution, or by a common or relative filter. `read_execution`.
- `list_executions` (numeric TestOps IDs) and `list_execution_outputs` (TestCloud string IDs and artifact URLs).
- `update_test_results` records a manual result or reviews an automated one.
- `prepare_artifact_upload` and `confirm_artifact_upload` attach evidence up to 10 MiB.

Quality metrics
- `fetch_requirement_metrics`, `fetch_defect_metrics`, `fetch_test_case_metrics`, `fetch_test_configuration_metrics`.
- `fetch_test_stability_metrics` returns flaky, always failing, newly failing, and slow tests. It takes a lookback window. It has no minimum run count.

Test Execution - Cloud assets and tunnels
- `list_test_cloud_environments`, `list_test_cloud_agents`, `list_test_cloud_apps`.
- `get_upload_test_cloud_app_url`, `create_test_cloud_app`, `manage_test_cloud_dynamic_app`, `delete_test_cloud_app`.
- `list_test_cloud_tunnels`, `prepare_test_cloud_tunnel_start`, `stop_test_cloud_tunnel`.

TrueTest
- `list_truetest_auts`, `list_truetest_tracking_environments`, `search_truetest_sessions`, `get_truetest_session`.
- `search_truetest_journey_maps`, `get_truetest_journey_map`, `create_truetest_journey_map`, `get_truetest_journey_map_request`.
- `create_truetest_test_case_from_session` takes 1 to 25 sessions. `create_truetest_test_case_from_flow` takes one journey-map flow. Both queue generation and need user approval. A flow that already has linked cases follows the backend regeneration behavior, so confirm before you run it there.

Team memory (Kai)
- `memory_list`, `memory_read`, `memory_read_page` read the conventions the team and the user taught Kai.
- `memory_write` and `memory_forget` change that memory. Call them only when the user asks to remember or forget something. Memory is optional context. Every skill works when it is empty or unavailable.

## Not available through the MCP

- Create requirements. Create them in Jira or Azure DevOps, then sync, find, and link.
- Create a formal Test Plan entity. A named folder or suite gives an execution scope. It is no plan of record.
- Guarantee that Run with AI finishes. The platform can block it or fail it.
- Stop a running automated execution (Studio, Katalon Test Execution - Local, or Test Execution - Cloud). `rerun_execution` starts a new one. To close a TestPak run, including a hosted Run with AI session, call `update_test_run` with END.
- Inspect the live AUT. Use a browser tool or Playwright.
- Look up another user to set an assignee.
- Look up a manual run by its order number. Find the numeric `execution_id` with `list_executions`, then call `read_execution`.
- Create or edit suite collections.
- Author release gates, custom fields, tags, Git repository settings, project governance, or project-wide agent rules. Use the True Platform UI.
- Self-healing and Time Capsule. These are product features outside the MCP.
- Create a defect without a failed test result ID and ALM integration details.

## Quirks every skill keeps

- `delete_test_case` removes a case. Ask for a yes that names the case. Read back after the delete.
- A test case name starts with a letter or digit. It accepts letters, digits, spaces, and `( ) . , _ -`. The characters `@ : /` are rejected. A `path` for a case starts with `Test Cases`. A folder path can contain `/`.
- `create_test_case` with type AUTOMATED creates nothing. It returns guidance only.
- `update_test_cases` with UPDATE_CONTENT replaces all steps. Send the complete step list and keep every Call Test Case step.
- `manage_test_suite` rejects a suite that mixes MANUAL and AUTOMATED cases.
- Two ID spaces both say "execution". TestOps uses a number. TestCloud uses a string. No tool converts one to the other. Never swap `list_executions` and `list_execution_outputs`. `update_test_run` takes the platform `execution_id`. It never takes `manualExecutionId` or the order number shown in the UI.
- `update_test_results` counts as success only when the outcome is `applied` or `unchanged`. A manual result needs an active run that the caller created. An automated review needs a completed run.
- Run with AI asks for `browser_profile_mode` (SHARED or SEPARATE). The legacy launcher also asks for `os` (windows or linux). Ask the user. Never infer either. Hosted AI runs Chrome on Windows or Linux only.
- `update_test_run` with START needs a choice between Run with AI and manual testing in TestPak. If the user did not choose, ask. A missing AI request does not select MANUAL.
- `create_defect` needs `alm_integration_id` and `alm_connection_id` from `list_alm_integrations`. It also needs a `summary`. Ask the user for it. Check `fetch_defects` first to avoid a duplicate.
- `search_truetest_sessions` covers at most 31 days. A `session_reference` is opaque. Never build one by hand.
- `search` tier (exact, strong, weak) decides whether something exists. A response with `incomplete=true`, `retrieval_mode="keyword_fallback"`, or a warning never proves absence. Assets created in the last few minutes may be missing.
- Resource links in tool results may point to a host that does not resolve for your tenant. Give the ID as well as the link.

## Terminology

Katalon True Platform was TestOps. Katalon Test Execution - Local was Katalon Runtime Engine (KRE). Katalon Test Execution - Cloud was TestCloud. On first mention, give both names. After that, use the current name.

### references/generation-and-review.md

# Generation and review

Read this when the user has approved a list of sessions or a flow and you queue case generation. The parameter lists come from the live tool schemas captured on 2026-10-20.

## The two tools

| Tool | Takes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `create_truetest_test_case_from_session` | `project_id`, `client_code`, `tracking_environment_id`, and 1 to 25 `session_references` | Search with the same `tracking_environment_id` first. Pass only the references the user selected, unchanged. The service queues TrueTest automated test generation. |
| `create_truetest_test_case_from_flow` | `project_id`, `client_code`, `map_id`, `flow_id`, optional `tags` (up to 20) and `include_test_case_id_prefix` (default true) | A flow with linked cases follows the backend regeneration behavior. |

Both tools queue work. Neither returns the cases.

## Approval gates

1. Present the exact sessions (table in `SKILL.md`) or the exact flow.
2. Get a yes that names them. Follow `references/write-policy.md`.
3. For a flow that already has linked cases, say that generation follows the backend regeneration behavior. Get a second yes.
4. Call the tool once. A yes covers one call. A larger set splits into batches of 25 or fewer, each with its own yes.

Without a yes, stop.

## Outcomes

| Result | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `STARTED` | The request was accepted or queued. | Report it as queued. Never report cases as created. |
| `TERMINATE` (flow tool) | No request was created. | Report it. Ask the user. Do not retry on your own. |
| An error | Nothing is known about the state. | Report it. Read back before any retry, so you never create a duplicate request. |

No tool cancels a queued generation. Tell the user that before they approve a large batch.

## Read back

- **Flow path.** Call `get_truetest_journey_map` with `map_id` and `flow_id`. It reports current flow status and linked cases. It is the current state, not a history of one request.
- **Session path.** No tool returns the new cases for a request. Search with `find_test_cases` and `search` (`types` `["test_case"]`) by the feature and keywords of the sessions. Do not assume a folder.
- Recent cases may need a few minutes to appear. Hedge any claim that a case is missing.

## Review every generated case as a draft

1. **Check the type.** The service uses automated test generation. Read each case with `read_test_cases` (`content_type` `FLOW`) and note whether it is MANUAL or AUTOMATED. A suite rejects a mix of the two. Keep the types apart.
2. **Check the name.** A name starts with a letter or digit. It accepts letters, digits, spaces, and `( ) . , _ -`.
3. **Check for duplicates.** Compare the titles with existing cases. Reuse an existing case before you keep a new one.
4. **Check atomicity.** Split a case that checks more than one condition. Hand off to `create-test-cases` for the split.
5. **Check expected results.** A generated result copies observed behavior. Replace it with a requirement-backed result when one exists. Otherwise mark it "observed, unconfirmed".
6. **Check privacy.** Remove real names, emails, account numbers, and free text.
7. **Link requirements** once IDs are known. `create-test-cases` and `test-management` own that step.

Prefer `update_test_cases` over delete and recreate. `delete_test_case` is unreliable.

## Failure and partial results

If a call fails part way, stop. Report what changed and what did not. Do not retry blindly. Do not queue a second generation to replace a failed one before you read back.

### references/journey-maps.md

# Journey maps

Read this when the user wants coverage of whole journeys. A journey map groups captured sessions into pages, flows, steps, and transitions. The parameter lists come from the live tool schemas captured on 2026-10-20.

## Choose a map

`search_truetest_journey_maps` needs `project_id` and `client_code`. Filters:

| Filter | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `status` | `active`, `archived`, `generating`, or `error`. Start with `active`. |
| `tracking_environment_id` | The environment the user chose. |
| `tracked_data_start_time`, `tracked_data_end_time` | The traffic window the map covers. |
| `created_from`, `created_to`, `creator_email` | Who built it and when. |

The result gives summaries and a `web_url`. Give the user the `web_url` when a visual review helps. Copy `map_id` unchanged into the next call. Pick the map whose tracked window matches the question. A map that is `generating` is not ready. A map in `error` needs a new build, after the user agrees.

## Read a map

`get_truetest_journey_map` needs `project_id`, `client_code`, and `map_id`. It never changes anything. Viewing a map does not approve a review, retry failures, archive data, alter flows, or generate cases.

The response holds four lists that each have a page limit and a page token:

| List | Limit argument | Token argument |
|---|---|---|
| Flows | `flow_limit` (1 to 25, default 10) | `flow_page_token` |
| Steps | `step_limit` (1 to 100, default 20) | `step_page_token` |
| Transitions | `transition_limit` (1 to 100, default 50) | `transition_page_token` |
| Pages | `page_limit` (1 to 100, default 50) | `page_page_token` |

Page each list on its own. A token from one list does not work for another. Pass `flow_id` to read one exact flow. Copy `flow_id` from an earlier response, never build it.

The response supports journey, traffic, coverage, and saved-assertion views. Read the field names it returns. Do not assume a field that the response lacks.

## Compare flows with existing cases

1. List the flows. Note traffic and any linked cases the map reports for each.
2. For a flow with no linked case, call `find_test_cases` by feature area and keyword, and `search` with `types` `["test_case"]` and `include_documents` false. A case may cover the flow without a link.
3. A `search` response with `incomplete=true`, `retrieval_mode="keyword_fallback"`, or a warning never proves absence. Recent cases may be missing for a few minutes.
4. Sort each flow into covered, partly covered, or uncovered. Rank the uncovered flows by traffic. Say how you judged each one.

## Build a map

Build a map only when no suitable one exists. `create_truetest_journey_map` writes. It starts an async job.

Required: `project_id`, `client_code`, `tracking_environment_id` (UUID from `list_truetest_tracking_environments`), `start_time_from`, `start_time_to`.

Optional: `session_attributes` (flat string filters), `url_keywords` (literal text, never regex), `carry_over_annotations` (default true), `compare_with_previous_map` (default true).

Preview all of it. Keep both flags at their default unless the user says otherwise. Get a yes. Call once.

## Poll the job

1. Report the build as queued. Keep the returned `request_id`.
2. Call `get_truetest_journey_map_request` with that exact `request_id`. It gives the request-to-map correlation.
3. Poll at a calm pace. If the job is still pending after several polls, give the user the `request_id` and stop. Offer to check later.
4. When it completes, copy the correlated `map_id` unchanged into `get_truetest_journey_map`.

## Never resubmit

After a validation error, conflict, timeout, or upstream error, report what happened. Do not call `create_truetest_journey_map` again on your own. A second call can start a duplicate job.

After a timeout with no `request_id`, call `search_truetest_journey_maps` with `status` `generating` and the same environment. That shows whether the job started. Then ask the user how to go on.

### references/session-selection.md

# Session selection

Read this when you search TrueTest sessions for coverage work. The parameter list comes from the live tool schemas captured on 2026-10-20. Check the tool schema before you rely on a parameter.

## Identity rules

- The AUT identity is `platform_aut_id` together with `client_code`, both from `list_truetest_auts`.
- `project_id` is the Katalon True Platform (formerly TestOps) project. `test_project_id` is the repository. `aut_project_id` is only the link record. Do not mix them.
- The server rejects an AUT that is not linked to the project.

## Search arguments

`search_truetest_sessions` needs `project_id`, `client_code`, `start_time`, and `end_time`. Times are UTC with an offset, such as `2026-07-01T00:00:00Z`.

| Argument | Use it for | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `start_time`, `end_time` | The window | At most 31 days. Use the narrowest range that answers the question. |
| `tracking_environment_id` | Attributes, flow metadata, replay link | Pass it whenever you plan to generate from the result. Without it the search covers all permitted environments and adds none of these fields. |
| `url_patterns` | A page or path | Literal text, not regex. At most 10 values. |
| `attributes` | A known custom attribute | A list of `{name, value, match}`. Prefer `EQUALS`. Use only attribute names you know. |
| `minimum_step_count`, `maximum_step_count` | Long journeys or short ones | Inclusive. Use a minimum to skip bounces. |
| `domain` | One site | Exact value, no protocol or path. |
| `session_id` | One known session | The user-visible ID. It is never the internal replay key. |
| `email` | Locating one person's session | Use only when the user explicitly asks. |
| `limit` | Page size | 1 to 25. Default 20. |
| `poll_timeout_seconds` | Wait for the async search | 1 to 60. Default 30. |

## Paging

The search is async on the server. A result may carry `next_page_token`. Pass that value as `page_token` and repeat every other argument unchanged. A changed argument breaks the page chain. Start a new search instead.

## Reading one session

Call `get_truetest_session` with `project_id`, `client_code`, and one `session_reference`. The default response holds metadata and ordered replay steps. Leave `include_raw_events` false. Set it to true only for an explicit troubleshooting request. It returns at most 100 events and does not redact field values.

## Never build a reference

A `session_reference` is opaque. Pass it exactly as `search_truetest_sessions` returned it. Never build one from a session ID, a replay URL, or a timestamp. The same rule holds for `flow_id` and `map_id`.

## Triage

Keep a session when it shows a distinct path that real users take. Drop it when it is:

- a duplicate of a path you already kept,
- a bot or a health check,
- a one-off error with no pattern behind it,
- too short to hold a meaningful check, such as a bounce.

Prefer sessions with a mix of common and rare paths over 25 copies of the same flow. Give each kept session one line that says what the user did and what case it would yield.

## Privacy

Mask names, emails, account numbers, and free text before you quote anything. Use reserved values such as `@example.com`. Never paste replay content into a case without a check.

### references/write-policy.md

<!-- GENERATED from shared/references/write-policy.md - edit the source -->
# Write Policy, Execution Consent, and Session Rules

These rules apply to every agent and every skill that changes data on Katalon True Platform (formerly TestOps).

## Write policy

1. Resolve the project and repository first.
2. Preview the full mutation set in chat. List each create, update, move, link, and delete with its target.
3. Ask for one confirmation for the whole set.
4. Run the writes.
5. Read back each changed item with a read tool and report what the platform now holds.

Reads need no confirmation. This covers every tool that finds, reads, lists, gets, fetches, searches, or lists metrics, every memory read tool, and every tool that only builds a payload.

A user who says "go ahead and do all of it" has confirmed the set you previewed. A new write outside that set needs a new preview.

Destructive tools need an explicit yes that names the target. These are:
- `delete_test_case`.
- `delete_test_cloud_app`. The user types YES. Confirm which app when several match.
- `manage_test_folder` or `manage_test_suite` with a DELETE action. Resolve the exact folder `id` with `find_test_folders` by its full `rawPath`.
- `stop_test_cloud_tunnel`. It stops a tunnel that other runs may share.
- `manage_test_cloud_dynamic_app` with an UPDATE action. UPDATE silently redirects every consumer of the app alias.
- `manage_requirement_test_case_linkages` with `action` set to `unlink`. Name the links.
- `update_test_run` with END and `unfinished_cases` set to `SKIP`. SKIP also stops hosted AI.
- `memory_forget`. It deletes for good. Call it only when the user asks to forget something. Name what you deleted.

`memory_write` stores a note in the user's own words. Call it only when the user asks you to remember something. A project-wide rule belongs on the Agent Rules screen, which needs a project admin.

Other writes need a preview and a yes of their own:
- `prepare_artifact_upload` and `confirm_artifact_upload` put a file where every project member can see it. Preview the filename, the exact byte size, the mime type, and the visibility (shared with project members). Confirm once, then prepare, upload, and confirm. Call them only when the user asked to attach evidence. Mask personal data first. Never upload secrets.
- `create_defect` files a real Jira or Azure DevOps bug. Ask for the summary when it is missing. Preview the summary and description. Check `fetch_defects` for a linked defect first.
- `create_truetest_test_case_from_session` and `create_truetest_test_case_from_flow` queue generation. `STARTED` means queued, not done.
- `update_schedule_configuration` runs once, after the user confirms, with every target in one `updates` list and only the settings the user asked for.

Two more rules for bulk work:
- Before a bulk write, run the plan and validation steps first. Check names, folder paths, and duplicates against what already exists. Then write.
- If a write fails part way, stop. Report which items changed and which did not. Do not retry blindly. Do not create a duplicate to replace a failed create. Search first.

## Execution consent

Confirm before you call `create_test_run`, `update_test_run` with START, `create_manual_ai_session`, or `rerun_execution`. These calls use Test Execution - Cloud minutes, launch a hosted browser, or can change data in the application under test (AUT). Creating a TestPak for later, with no START, still needs the preview. The confirmation names:
- the suite or cases,
- the AUT environment,
- the mode (manual, Run with AI, or automated),
- the schedule if one exists,
- and any private network setup.

A confirmation covers one run. Ask again for the next run.

## Stateless MCP

The MCP specification of 2026-07-28 removes protocol sessions. Clients differ in elicitation and sampling support.
- Never rely on a server prompt or on sampling. Ask the user in chat.
- Carry IDs between calls yourself. Repeat `project_id` and `repository_id` on every call that takes them.
- Prefer structured fields in a tool result. If they are missing, parse the text block.
- Treat a tool annotation such as "read-only" as a hint. It is no safety argument. Follow this policy.

## Terminology

Katalon True Platform (formerly TestOps). Katalon Test Execution - Local (formerly Katalon Runtime Engine, KRE). Katalon Test Execution - Cloud (formerly TestCloud). On first mention, give both names. Use one name for one thing after that.
